howto.name: Upload an audio file
howto.text: Drop MP3, WAV, AAC, FLAC, OGG, or M4A — up to 200 MB.

howto.name: Set start and end
howto.text: Type the start and end timestamps in HH:MM:SS format (e.g. 00:01:30 to 00:02:45).

howto.name: Click Trim audio
howto.text: Stream-copy preserves the original quality — no re-encoding, except that FLAC is rewritten losslessly.

faq.q: How precise are the start/end times?
faq.a: Times can be set to the millisecond. Because the audio is copied rather than re-encoded, a cut lands on the nearest compressed-audio frame, within a few hundredths of a second. Trim Media copies audio the same way.
No — we use stream-copy mode which preserves the original audio bytes. The trimmed file is identical quality to the source.
Same format as input. Trim an MP3 → get an MP3. Trim a FLAC → get a FLAC, rewritten losslessly; every other format is copied without re-encoding.

No. The title, artist, album, dates and comments are left out, and so are any location and device details a phone or recorder stored. In MP3 and M4A files the chapter markers inside the cut keep their titles and move with it, and M4A and OGG files keep the track's language.
